elements.element: No minimum purchase commitment imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer commits to purchase no minimum amount of Services"

elements.element: Fees payable only for usage or ordered Services
elements.evidence: "and pays only for Services ordered or used"
take-or-pay language deleted; replaced by "pays only for Services ordered or used"

elements.element: Commitment limited to the current 12-month term
elements.evidence: clause states "in each of the next three years" but with "no minimum amount"; no 12-month-term commitment exists
no reduction-notice mechanic in operative text (only in non-operative margin comment)

elements.element: True-up rather than penalty on shortfall
elements.evidence: no true-up language in the operative clause

reasons: The redline achieves the locked preferred level: the USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment is eliminated ("no minimum amount") and payment is expressly limited to Services ordered or used.
Change is confined to the single offending sentence in 2.1; Section 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement is left untouched and now consistent, so no contradiction or dangling mechanic arises.

Fallback elements (12-month cap, 30-day reduction right, true-up) are absent from the operative text, but they are unnecessary because no commitment survives; the fallback is offered only in the non-operative comment, which is appropriate.
Residual phrase "in each of the next three years" is harmless surplus retained from the original and does not create an obligation, so minimality is preserved.
